summary.text: Dennis Conlon is a retired analytical chemist and former product-development principal scientist running as an Unenrolled candidate for Massachusetts's 3rd District.
He says his campaign is self-funded and takes no outside contributions, and that he collected over 2,200 signatures himself to qualify for the ballot.
He describes himself as 73 and says he would be content with one term.

paragraphs.text: Conlon earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Massachusetts in 1976, an MBA from Providence College in 1993, and, according to BallotReady, a certificate in biopharmaceutical engineering from the University of Massachusetts Lowell in 2007.

He describes a 43.5-year career as an analytical chemist, most recently as a principal scientist in product development for a medical device manufacturer, and says he holds 9 U.S. patents as an inventor.

BallotReady lists his work history as senior scientist at Bayer Diagnostics (1976-1999), principal scientist at Instrumentation Laboratory (1999-2019), and QC laboratory technician at Cytiva (2021-2022).
In his Ballotpedia survey responses, Conlon says he has been married 45 years.
